newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber-Prices seen steady to firm on stock hopes.
newsitem.headline: Rubber-Prices seen steady to firm on stock hopes.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures markets are likely to be steady to slightly firmer this week, supported by expectations that excessive domestic stockpiles may at last start to fall, traders said on Tuesday.
The rubber market could also be helped by attempts to correct recent oversold conditions, they said.

Many traders believe that some Japanese traders will take physical deliveries when spot rubber contracts on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) and the Kobe Rubber Exchange expire on May 26, and sell the warehouse supplies to China.
Some Japanese traders signed a contract last month to sell a total of 1,200 tonnes of rubber to China.

"A perception is growing in the market that Japan's rubber stocks have nearly reached a peak," an analyst with a commodity brokerage house said. "Inventories may fall and fading concern over near-term oversupply trends could stimulate short-covering this week," he said.

Japanese traders have been recently holding back purchases of rubber from producing countries because domestic rubber prices are low relative to overseas prices, another factor likely to contribute to easier stockpiles, traders said.
The benchmark October rubber futures contract on TOCOM ended the Tuesday morning session at 142.1 yen per kg, up from Friday's close of 141.5 yen.
Benchmark October on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was also firmer, standing at 142.9 yen per kg at midday after closing at 141.9 yen on Friday.
The markets were closed on Monday for a national holiday.
Although the outlook is slightly brighter, traders say a full recovery is unlikely in view of relatively high stock levels and a dearth of strong buying incentives.
The topside level of 145 yen will be hard to break as selling is waiting above the level, they said.
Japanese rubber stocks stood at 40,669 tonnes as of April 20, according to the Rubber Trade Association of Japan, far above appropriate levels of around 25,000 tonnes.
"It is too early to say that rubber markets have entered an upward trend amid a lack of fresh incentives," an analyst with another commodity brokerage said.
"The expected rise this week would be considered a technical reaction after the TOCOM benchmark hit a recent low of 133.6 yen on April 23," the analyst said.
Thai rubber to Japan was offered at 108 U.S. cents per kg on a FOB basis on Tuesday, unchanged from April 30.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 152 yen per kg on Tuesday, against 147 yen on April 30.
